A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Deep FlexQP work. Text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support reliable comparison. V2 adds an extended related-work appendix; v1 Appendices A–N otherwise correspond to v2 Appendices B–O.

before.justification: V1 reports original QP benchmark experiments, simulated trajectory optimization and safety-filter results, and architecture and loss ablations.

after.justification: V2 retains these original empirical results and additionally reports qualitative findings from comparing fine-tuning losses on large-scale QPs.

M1.justification: Equation 9 and Algorithm 1 correct the dual updates to include the relaxation terms omitted in v1. The relaxation-policy formula also replaces a duplicated slack residual with the equality residual (v1 Equation 40; v2 Equation 32). These are localized corrections to the documented procedure; the PDFs do not establish corresponding implementation changes.

E1.justification: Table 1 and the experimental appendices retain the same random QPs, finance and regression/classification problems, linear-control systems, large-scale portfolio/SVM problems, nonlinear vehicle and quadrotor tasks, and predictive safety-filter scenarios.

E2.justification: The corresponding comparisons retain OSQP, FlexQP, Deep OSQP, Deep OSQP—RLQP Parameterization, and Deep OSQP—Improved. SQP with OSQP and Shield-MPPI remain the control-task baselines. The added loss comparison changes training controls, not solver membership.

E3.justification: Section 5.2 newly reports a controlled comparison that fine-tunes each learned method using either Equation 11 or Equation 12. Existing benchmark sample counts, budgets, metrics, and convergence tolerances remain unchanged. Newly supplied learning-rate and batch-size information does not establish changes to existing runs.

E4.justification: V2 Section 5.2 adds a qualitative loss ablation investigating whether the large-scale fine-tuning advantage comes from the training objective. Existing LSTM-versus-MLP, Deep FlexQP loss, parameter-trajectory, and generalization-bound analyses are retained across the renumbered appendices.

E5.justification: The averaging and error-bar practices remain unchanged. The PAC-Bayes estimation procedure still uses 10,000 model samples and a 99% probability guarantee (v1 Appendix L; v2 Appendix M). No new seed information, repeated-run counts, or significance tests are reported.

E6.justification: Section 5.2 adds findings that the two fine-tuning losses perform comparably on portfolio problems, while the multiplier loss performs worse for Deep OSQP variants on large-scale SVMs. Existing numerical results and plotted curves are retained, including Deep FlexQP's 15.3-second and 43.4-second solve times in Figure 6.

T1.justification: Section 2 strengthens the stated smoothness requirement for the constraints from differentiable to twice differentiable. Theorem 3.3's proof corrects the negative soft-thresholding case from a positive to a negative threshold (v1 Appendix E; v2 Appendix F). The main theorem statements and PAC-Bayes bounds are retained.

C1.justification: V2 refines the headline claims by explicitly identifying convex QPs, the convergence assumption, and large-scale scaling through fine-tuning. Its abstract adds quantitative SQP and safety-filter claims supported by retained results. The central solver, learned acceleration, and generalization-certificate contributions remain.

C2.justification: V1 Section 5.2 attributes the fine-tuning advantage primarily to the normalized multiplier loss. V2 replaces this hypothesis with an architectural explanation emphasizing elastic relaxation and LSTMs, motivated by the newly reported loss comparison. This changes the proposed mechanism without independently isolating those architectural effects.

D1.justification: V2 Section 5 newly specifies dense batched implementation, a learning rate of 10^-3, and a default batch size of 50. Large-scale batch size 1 was already documented in v1. The RTX 4090 specification remains, but the Intel i9-13900K CPU specification is removed.

R1.justification: New Appendix A substantially expands positioning across QP solvers, penalty methods, ADMM, SQP, deep unfolding, and learned-optimizer guarantees. Added discussions distinguish FlexQP from SCS/COSMO infeasibility detection and compare its certificates with other guarantee frameworks. This is a substantial literature expansion beyond bibliographic updates.

P1.justification: V2 rewrites the abstract and conclusion, condenses Section 4.1 while retaining detailed policy formulas in the appendix, adds an experimental overview, and corrects explanatory wording. The six-section main narrative remains in the same order; the principal structural addition is the related-work appendix.

P2.justification: The document is extensively reformatted into the ICLR layout, with new typography and running headers, wrapped figures, compact equation arrangements, and a boxed Equation 9. Figure 11 and Figures 16–17 redistribute panels across pages, and tables are relocated. These are broad presentation changes while the underlying visual evidence is retained.

improvement.justification: V2 improves internal consistency through algorithm and proof corrections, supplies useful training details, and supports its revised fine-tuning interpretation with an additional loss comparison. Expanded related work clarifies the contribution's position. The gains are limited: the empirical results largely remain unchanged, the new comparison is qualitative, and the CPU specification is lost.
